## How to use this

The code from Lecture 25, run, with the numbers it produces, and the migration
exercise solved.

. . .

`lmer()` and `glmer()` find their answers numerically, so your last decimal
place may differ slightly from these.

::: {.notes}
Posted after class so nobody is left wondering whether their answer was right.
:::

## Songbirds: set up and fit {.smaller}

```{r}
library(lme4)
library(bbmle)
library(biometrydata)

songbirds <- avonet[avonet$Order1 == "Passeriformes", ]
birds <- data.frame(species = songbirds$Species1,
                    family = songbirds$Family1,
                    hwi = songbirds$Hand.Wing.Index,
                    lat = abs(songbirds$Centroid.Latitude),
                    migratory = as.numeric(songbirds$Migration == 3))
birds <- na.omit(birds)
c(species = nrow(birds), families = length(unique(birds$family)))

lm_lat <- lm(hwi ~ lat, data = birds)
mm_lat <- lmer(hwi ~ lat + (1 | family), data = birds)
coef(lm_lat)
fixef(mm_lat)
```

## Reading the output {.smaller}

```{r}
VarCorr(mm_lat)

# share of the variation that is between families
vc <- as.data.frame(VarCorr(mm_lat))
vc$vcov[1] / sum(vc$vcov)

# standard errors of the latitude slope
c(lm = summary(lm_lat)$coefficients["lat", 2],
  lmer = summary(mm_lat)$coefficients["lat", 2])
```

## Compare, and get intervals {.smaller}

```{r}
mm_lat_ml  <- lmer(hwi ~ lat + (1 | family), data = birds, REML = FALSE)
mm_null_ml <- lmer(hwi ~ 1 + (1 | family), data = birds, REML = FALSE)
AICtab(lm_lat, mm_null_ml, mm_lat_ml)

confint(mm_lat_ml)     # .sig01 is the family standard deviation, .sigma the residual
```

## Your turn: two rules of biogeography {.smaller}

```{r}
rules <- data.frame(family = songbirds$Family1,
                    lat = abs(songbirds$Centroid.Latitude),
                    mass = songbirds$Mass,
                    range = songbirds$Range.Size)
rules <- na.omit(rules)

lm_mass <- lm(log(mass) ~ lat, data = rules)
mm_mass <- lmer(log(mass) ~ lat + (1 | family), data = rules)
lm_range <- lm(log(range) ~ lat, data = rules)
mm_range <- lmer(log(range) ~ lat + (1 | family), data = rules)

# share of the variation between families
vc <- as.data.frame(VarCorr(mm_mass)); vc$vcov[1] / sum(vc$vcov)
vc <- as.data.frame(VarCorr(mm_range)); vc$vcov[1] / sum(vc$vcov)
```

## Two rules: the latitude slopes {.smaller}

```{r}
confint(lm_mass)["lat", ]
confint(mm_mass, parm = "lat", quiet = TRUE)
c(lm = coef(lm_range)[["lat"]], lmer = fixef(mm_range)[["lat"]])
exp(10 * fixef(mm_range)["lat"])    # range multiplier per 10 degrees
```

Body mass runs strongly in families, range size barely does, so `lmer()` barely
changes the range answer: ranges are about 1.8 times larger every 10 degrees from
the equator. Neither model finds Bergmann's rule: both mass intervals include
zero.

## Small families borrow from big ones {.smaller}

```{r}
mm0 <- lmer(hwi ~ 1 + (1 | family), data = birds)
raw <- tapply(birds$hwi, birds$family, mean)
est <- coef(mm0)$family[names(raw), 1]
n <- as.vector(table(birds$family)[names(raw)])

shrink <- data.frame(n = n, raw = round(raw, 1), est = round(est, 1))
shrink[c("Eupetidae", "Peucedramidae", "Tyrannidae", "Thraupidae"), ]
fixef(mm0)      # the overall average they are pulled toward
```

## Bobwhite: set up and fit {.smaller}

```{r}
bw <- bobwhite_counts
bw$route <- factor(bw$route)
bw$decade <- bw$elapsed / 10
c(counts = nrow(bw), routes = length(unique(bw$route)))

g_nb <- MASS::glm.nb(count ~ decade, data = bw)
mm_pois <- glmer(count ~ decade + (1 | route), family = poisson, data = bw)
mm_nb <- glmer.nb(count ~ decade + (1 | route), data = bw)
AICtab(g_nb, mm_pois, mm_nb)
```

## Bobwhite: inside the 95% range {.smaller}

Lecture 24's check, for each model:

```{r}
inside <- function(lo, hi){
  mean(bw$count >= lo & bw$count <= hi)
}
mu <- fitted(g_nb)
c(g_nb = inside(qnbinom(0.025, mu = mu, size = g_nb$theta),
                qnbinom(0.975, mu = mu, size = g_nb$theta)))
mu <- fitted(mm_pois)
c(mm_pois = inside(qpois(0.025, mu), qpois(0.975, mu)))
theta <- getME(mm_nb, "glmer.nb.theta")
mu <- fitted(mm_nb)
c(mm_nb = inside(qnbinom(0.025, mu = mu, size = theta),
                 qnbinom(0.975, mu = mu, size = theta)))
```

## Undo the link {.smaller}

```{r}
b <- fixef(mm_nb)["decade"]
exp(b)                         # per decade
exp(b / 10)                    # per year

ci <- confint(mm_nb, parm = "beta_", method = "Wald")
exp(ci["decade", ] / 10)

exp(coef(g_nb)["decade"] / 10) # ignoring routes: Lecture 15's 2.9% a year
```

A bobwhite route loses about 3.9% of its birds each year (3.4% to 4.3%), against
2.9% when every count is treated as independent.

## Why is the decline steeper? {.smaller}

```{r}
# each route's intercept, attached to its counts
re <- ranef(mm_nb)$route
bw$route_effect <- re[as.character(bw$route), 1]

# routes counted each year, and how good they are, as a multiplier on an average route
yearly <- data.frame(routes = tapply(bw$route, bw$year, function(x){ length(unique(x)) }),
                     quality = round(exp(tapply(bw$route_effect, bw$year, mean)), 2))
yearly[c("1997", "2001", "2010", "2015", "2019"), ]
```

Fewer routes in later years, and the ones left are the better routes, so the
average count across all routes falls more slowly than the count on any one
route.

## Your turn: does development explain the routes? {.smaller}

```{r}
g_built <- MASS::glm.nb(count ~ decade + frac_built, data = bw)
mm_built <- glmer.nb(count ~ decade + frac_built + (1 | route), data = bw)

rbind(g_built = summary(g_built)$coefficients["frac_built", 1:2],
      mm_built = summary(mm_built)$coefficients["frac_built", 1:2])
VarCorr(mm_nb)
VarCorr(mm_built)
AICtab(mm_nb, mm_built)
1 - exp(fixef(mm_built)["frac_built"] / 10)   # fewer birds per 10 points of built land
```

The estimate barely moves but its standard error grows about 2.6 times:
`frac_built` has one value per route, so the counts hold about 100 pieces of
evidence about it, not 1,360. It also explains part of why routes differ.

## Each route its own rate {.smaller}

```{r}
mm_slope <- glmer.nb(count ~ decade + (1 + decade | route), data = bw)
AICtab(mm_nb, mm_slope)
VarCorr(mm_slope)

b <- fixef(mm_slope)["decade"]
s <- as.data.frame(VarCorr(mm_slope))$sdcor[2]
exp(c(average = b, low = b - 1.96 * s, high = b + 1.96 * s) / 10)   # per year
```

## The average route is not every route {.smaller}

```{r}
route_change <- exp(coef(mm_slope)$route[, "decade"] / 10) - 1   # each route, per year
range(route_change)
sum(route_change > 0)                         # shrunk estimates above zero
pnorm(0, mean = b, sd = s, lower.tail = FALSE) # share of routes the model expects to be rising
```

The average route declines, but not every route does: about 1 route in 9 is
expected to be gaining birds.

## Your turn: migration, with families {.smaller}

```{r}
g_add <- glm(migratory ~ lat + hwi, family = binomial, data = birds)
mm_mig <- glmer(migratory ~ lat + hwi + (1 | family), family = binomial, data = birds)

# odds ratios
cbind(glm = exp(coef(g_add)), glmer = exp(fixef(mm_mig)))[-1, ]

# standard errors
cbind(glm = summary(g_add)$coefficients[, 2],
      glmer = summary(mm_mig)$coefficients[, 2])[-1, ]

# for anyone fast
AICtab(g_add, mm_mig)
```

## Your turn, in biology {.smaller}

Both standard errors grow, by about 1.5 times for latitude and 2.4 times for
HWI: the glm() treated 6,583 species as independent evidence, and relatives are
not, so it was too sure. Within a family, the species with more pointed wings
are much more likely to migrate: the odds ratio per unit of HWI rises from 1.08
to 1.17. And family is worth including: it wins by more than 470 AIC units.
